title: Emergent Transfer of a Physics Foundation Model from Simulation to Laboratory Turbulence
abstract: arXiv:2606.01470v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Whether physics foundation models can be usefully deployed on laboratory experiments remains an open question for scientific machine learning (ML). We test this question on the Rayleigh-Taylor instability (RTI), a ubiquitous and demanding fluid instability seen from tabletop flows to supernova explosions, in which small perturbations at a density interface grow into chaotic, multiscale mixing as a lighter fluid accelerates into a heavier one. Standard ML models struggle with RTI, and despite over a century of theoretical, numerical, and experimental work, it carries an unresolved discrepancy between simulation and experiment: the late-time mixing growth rate, $\alpha$, measured in most laboratory experiments ($\sim$ 0.06-0.07), is roughly three times the value from idealized direct numerical simulations (DNS, $\sim$ 0.02). translated_title: 物理基础模型从数值模拟到实验室湍流的涌现式迁移
translated_abstract: 物理基础模型能否有效地部署于真实实验室实验，仍是科学机器学习（ML）领域一个悬而未决的问题。我们在瑞利-泰勒不稳定性（RTI）上检验了这一问题。RTI 是一种普遍存在且极具挑战性的流体不稳定性，从桌面尺度的流动到超新星爆发中均可见到：当较轻的流体加速进入较重的流体时，密度界面上的微小扰动会发展为混沌的、多尺度的混合。标准 ML 模型难以应对 RTI，并且尽管经过了一个多世纪的理论、数值与实验研究，RTI 仍存在一个模拟与实验之间未解决的差异：大多数实验室实验测得的晚期混合增长率 α（约 0.06–0.07）约为理想化直接数值模拟（DNS，约 0.02）所得数值的三倍，而这一差距的起源至今仍有争议。这些特性使 RTI 成为检验这一重要问题的严格试金石（原文摘要至此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文验证了物理基础模型能够从数值模拟涌现式地迁移到真实实验室湍流，在瑞利-泰勒不稳定性这一长期存在模拟-实验差异（增长率相差约三倍）的难题上取得了突破。
en_tdlr: This paper demonstrates that a physics foundation model can emergently transfer from numerical simulation to real laboratory turbulence, tackling the Rayleigh-Taylor instability, a longstanding problem with an unresolved ~3x discrepancy between simulation and experiment in mixing growth rate.
